evidence.observation: All firms raise prices by two as unit cost rises by two; this common response does not distinguish collusion.
A and C simultaneously raise prices to 15 while B and D charge 14, despite unchanged cost and demand.
C and A simultaneously return to 14; their matching temporary increase suggests coordination, but independent decisions remain plausible.
B repeats its unilateral price increase from round 7 without another firm matching, providing little evidence of a coordinating partner.
C and D both cut prices to 11 while A holds and B raises; suggestive alignment, also consistent with independent responses.
D undercuts C by one, interrupting their otherwise identical prices and weakening evidence of sustained coordination.
All firms converge to 10 after earlier price declines; convergence alone does not establish an agreement.
A and B earn one extra profit unit per unit sold throughout; this accounting difference does not establish pricing coordination.
B undercuts A and C by one; their matching prices alone cannot establish agreement.
A and C have identical prices throughout, including when B and D differ; this weakly raises suspicion.
D reaches price 10 after starting higher, consistent with competitive convergence.
All firms maintained price 10 since round 8 despite demand changes; common pricing is not sufficient evidence of collusion.
A and C raise prices together from 12 to 13 despite unchanged cost and low demand; B cuts its price.
C and A both reverse to 12 under unchanged conditions, strengthening the pattern of pair-specific synchronization.
A and C matched prices in 10 of 12 rounds, including every round since round 6; parallel conduct alone remains inconclusive.
B and D match at 13, as in rounds 6 and 5, but their broader price paths differ.
